clue.text: Go and collect a truck

definitions.meaning: to go and collect someone or something is to fetch them in a vehicle
a small open-backed lorry with low sides

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fetch a lorry from a depot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means fetching, and the noun names a light open-backed lorry.

clue.text: As captain, I must enter mark on flight plan

indicators.note: the letter I has to go into the other piece, so it is placed inside

parts.note: to plot is to mark a course on a chart or plan

explanation.surface: An airline captain insists on adding his own mark to the flight plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain of an aircraft is the person who flies it.

clue.text: Highest-category class is in centre of boat

indicators.note: the two short pieces sit inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
A is the top grade or category, as in A-list
CL is a standard abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: A first-class cabin is found in the middle of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round wicker boat covered with hide, used in Wales and Ireland.

clue.text: Regrettable as nurse died after accident

indicators.note: after an accident things are jumbled and broken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad hospital story: a nurse has died following an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwanted is regrettable, not wished for.

clue.text: Upset, not liking denouement

parts.note: to be off something is to have stopped liking it
the denouement of a story is its end

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed because they dislike how a story finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to give them offence; both verbs mean to hurt feelings.

clue.text: Decorative strip through block

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Decorative strip through block (5)' for FRILL: 'Decorative strip' defines it, but no reading of 'through block' gives FRILL (no hidden run or charade), likely an OCR misread of the words after 'through', and no scan or search gives the printed text.

clue.text: What food should be, each waiter's responsibility?

parts.note: a waiter looks after a table in a restaurant

explanation.surface: A restaurant manager wonders whether each waiter should take charge of the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Food ought to be fit to consume, which is the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Notes tumult causing postponement

parts.note: D and E are two notes of the musical scale
a ferment is a state of agitation or turmoil

explanation.surface: Unrest over some memos leads to a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A deferral is a putting off until later, a postponement.

clue.text: State of plants I had put inside

indicators.note: the contraction is placed within the word for plants

parts.note: flora is the plant life of a region
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A gardener describes the condition of their plants after putting them indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition, but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Women's task done initially by one group of workers

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word done is used

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the staff are the workers of an organisation

explanation.surface: A job was started by one team of employees.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff, the stick used in spinning, came to stand for women's work and the female side of a family.

clue.text: Punishing terms I can give him?

definitions.text: Punishing terms I can give him?

indicators.note: punishing treatment knocks things about, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A judge muses on the harsh sentence they can hand a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain or wrongdoer is the kind of person one might sentence harshly.

clue.text: Not moving supplies to drawer

parts.note: stocks are supplies held in reserve
a till is a cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper moves supplies over to the cash drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely motionless is the meaning of this compound adjective.

clue.text: Set stream on fire?

parts.note: read as one wish, setting a brook alight; one word means both set on fire and, in Scotland, a small stream

explanation.surface: An absurd attempt to ignite a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means set alight, and the Scottish noun means a small stream.

clue.text: Pure sound in clip

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for pure is said aloud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: sheer means pure or unmixed

explanation.surface: A recording clip contains a pure tone.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip wool or hedges is to cut it with blades.

clue.text: A very soft centre to cord used for binding

indicators.note: the short pieces are put at the centre of the word for cord

parts.note: string is thin cord
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A cord with a soft core is used to tie things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Strips of material for tying or bandaging are collectively called by this noun.

clue.text: Drove round the bend and left with no escape

definitions.meaning: a driver who has taken a bend has turned a corner
an animal or person trapped with no way out

explanation.surface: A getaway driver took the bend and found himself trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means turned a corner and also trapped in a place with no exit.

clue.text: Actor's part undergoes a grim transformation into lengthy waffle

indicators.note: a transformation changes the form, so the letters of a grim are rearranged

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An actor's part takes a dark turn into long-winded speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformation' rearranges A GRIM into RIGMA; the clue names the actor's part first, but it ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rambling story or procedure is a rigmarole, much like waffle.

clue.text: Ignored a new fabric

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone overlooked a new material.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin stiff transparent muslin is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: A way to be on horse

definitions.text: A way to be on horse

parts.note: ST, street, is a way or road
to ride is to sit on a horse and be carried

explanation.surface: Instruction on how to sit when mounted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on each side of a horse is the usual riding position.

clue.text: Using bribery, first to get at lifeboat

indicators.note: the first letter of the word get is taken

parts.note: a raft can serve as a lifeboat

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to bribes to be first onto a lifeboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt gain through bribes is called graft, especially in politics.

clue.text: Poison — expert kept working with it

indicators.note: the word for expert keeps the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an ace is an expert
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A poisoner is careful to keep working with the toxin.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood, a plant whose root yields a deadly poison.

clue.text: Notice the spinners are back

indicators.note: back tells us the word for spinners is written backwards

parts.note: tops are toys that spin

explanation.surface: Someone sees that the spinning toys have returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it.

clue.text: Look in brownish tin at first for fruit

indicators.note: the word for tin comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: the short word for look goes inside the colour

parts.note: taupe is a brownish-grey colour
lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: Inspect a brown can to find some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of melon with orange flesh and a ribbed rind.

clue.text: Clerical profession's destiny settled in church

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition says the clerical profession is the answer

indicators.note: the word for destiny settles inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: one's lot is one's destiny

explanation.surface: A priest's fate is decided inside his church.
explanation.definitionFit: The clergy as a body are known as the cloth, after clerical dress.

clue.text: Unhealthy-looking pie

definitions.meaning: a pastry case folded round a filling, as in a Cornish one

explanation.surface: Someone looks pale, or else is a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pallid, and the noun is a folded pastry with filling.

clue.text: Cheque protected by security code and metal bars

indicators.note: the word for cheque is enclosed by the security code

parts.note: a PIN is a personal identification number
a giro is a British payment cheque, especially a benefits one

explanation.surface: A cheque guarded by a code, and some metal bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude iron cast into oblong blocks, or pigs, from a blast furnace.

clue.text: Most saintly and very keen to suppress false accounts

indicators.note: the word for keen holds down the other piece inside it

parts.note: hot on something means very keen
lies are untrue accounts

explanation.surface: The most pious person is eager to hush up untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective meaning sacred or saintly.

clue.text: Massage the ego of German writer

indicators.note: to massage is to knead and work over, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Flattering a German author's self-esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: The great German poet and dramatist who wrote Faust.

clue.text: False belief I've found Pliny's last letter

parts.note: here's is what one says on producing something found

indicators.note: the final letter of the Roman name Pliny is taken

explanation.surface: Someone has discovered a final letter written by Pliny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' tempts as a piece of correspondence; it is a single letter of 'Pliny'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretical opinion runs against accepted doctrine.
